items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: Eddie and I got along fine

ctx.x: your time, it's all right; and I'll help you out as much as I can."

Well, we got along fine. Eddie and I got along fine, and everything was great, because I did not want to play first saxophone, and I would go to any length to teach him the parts or anything, because I did not want them parts. So Cootie had him to play first part. That's mainly why Cootie put him on the first part. But he had him on the first part, and playing all the solos... Now, you talk about somebody working, he had him playing all the solos, and he's doing his act, I mean himself, he's singin' -- and he's…

And he could sing. You know, he could sing the Blues. He's a showman. He's a real showman. He's real funny. But he looked funny anyway. But he used to tear up the house. He used to really tear up the house. And it ended up to find out he had (what you call those?) one of them complexes. He had a complex about himself.
